![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14224904/assets/cc9e723494b5d592b97ff1b4795eb1bc0ca7be0c4608591792eb2ac5515a9811.png)

The quarter-ellipse above is defined by the parametric equations 

$$
x=\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,y=3\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta .
$$

What is the domain of the parameter $\theta ?$
question.worked_solution:
The parametric equations of an ellipse centered at the origin with a horizontal radius of length $a$ and a vertical radius of length $b$ are

$$
x=a\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,y=b\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,\theta \in [0,2\pi ).
$$

In our case, $a=1$ and $b=3.$ Therefore, the parametric equations of the *full* ellipse are

$$
x=\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,y=3\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,\theta \in [0,2\pi ).
$$

To restrict the parameterization to a quarter-ellipse, we associate the parameter $\theta $ with the central angle formed by a point $(x,y)$ on the elipse and the $x$-axis. 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14224904/assets/6eeff954ea6f159a3bdc781361da094319bcf06a5365d12e894228bb172a16e6.png)

We can see that if we restrict $\theta $ to $[\frac{\pi }{2},\pi ]$, we get the quarter-ellipse.

Therefore, the parametric equations of the quarter-ellipse are 

$$
x=\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,y=3\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,\theta \in [\frac{\pi }{2},\pi ].
$$
